answer: The sources indicate that as of the latest ECDC/WHO review, there are six confirmed cases, two probable cases, zero suspected cases, and three deaths related to the MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak. The Hantavirus Tracker and Hantavirus Live Tracker also report six confirmed cases, two probable cases, zero suspected cases, and three deaths as of June 17, 2026. However, other sources like Hantavirus Live Map & Tracker 2026 show significantly higher numbers with 114 confirmed cases and nine deaths across 12 countries. The discrepancies in the data suggest varying levels of monitoring and reporting.

results.title: MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak - Wikipedia
results.content:
In April 2026, an outbreak of hantavirus infection caused by the Andes virus was identified on the Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius. There were ten confirmed cases and two suspected cases directly linked to the outbreak as of 22 May. There have been three deaths, two of which have been confirmed as caused by the Andes virus, the last on 2 May. By 11 May, all passengers had disembarked and been evacuated, many to their home countries for quarantine. On 2 July 2026, the World Health Organization officially declared the outbreak to be over, after the last close contact was released from quarantine. [...] Print/export

results.title: Deadly MV Hondius Hantavirus Outbreak Is Over, W.H.O. Says - The New York Times
results.content:
Supported by

# Deadly Hantavirus Cruise Ship Outbreak Is Over 3 Months Later, W.H.O. Says

The rodent-borne virus, which sickened passengers on the MV Hondius, killed three people, led to a race to find its origin and a global health alert.

The reported illnesses this spring initially looked like the spread of a typical stomach bug on a luxury ocean liner, but the situation quickly escalated to a fatal outbreak of hantavirus, a rare rodent-borne pathogen, leading to weekslong quarantines for the ship’s passengers and a global health alert.

But the outbreak is now over, the World Health Organization announced on Thursday. Overall, there were 12 confirmed cases and one probable case aboard the cruise ship, including three deaths. [...] The declaration was made after the final contact of a passenger completed a quarantine period and tested negative for the virus, said the health agency, which is part of the United Nations.

The announcement ended a three-month saga that had scientists scrambling to find the origins of a rare vector for hantavirus; crew members and passengers held captive on a luxury ship; and global health officials enforcing contact tracing and quarantine protocols.

The luxury cruise liner, MV Hondius, began its trip carrying 175 passengers and crew members from nearly two dozen countries as it left Ushuaia, an Argentine city, on April 1. The first passenger sickened by the virus died less than two weeks later.

results.content:
"I'm deeply grateful for Jan's cooperation and leadership as he navigated the ship through an extraordinary and scary journey," Tedros wrote. "Thank you, dear Jan, for steering your passengers towards safety."
 Jack Brewster

  Jack Brewster

  # WHO says outbreak is stabilizing as Netherlands reports new case

  The World Health Organization said Friday that the hantavirus outbreak linked to the MV Hondius is stabilizing, with no new deaths in 20 days.

  In a post on X, WHO Director-general Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the global total now stands at 12 cases, including three deaths — all of which occurred before May 2. [...] He added, "There are no new deaths reported since May 2. The total number of deaths remains three out of 13 reported cases so far. The situation remains stable. Passengers who got sick are receiving needed care, while others remain in quarantine."

Advertisement

Advertisement

Prior to the case reported in Spain, the most recent infection was in the Netherlands: A crew member who left the MV Hondius in Tenerife was repatriated home and has been isolating since.

All passengers and crew are now in quarantine with close monitoring, Tedros previously said, and WHO surveillance will continue until the incubation period ends for everyone who was on board. [...] Posting on X, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also said there had been no new deaths reported since May 2.
 Jack Brewster

  Jack Brewster

  # MV Hondius captain disembarks symptom-free, Tedros says

  The captain of the MV Hondius, Jan Dobrogowski, finally left the cruise ship Saturday and remains free of hantavirus symptoms, World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said.

  In a post on X, Tedros said he had just received Dobrogowski's "last message" from the ship, which docked in Rotterdam earlier this week for disinfection. All passengers and crew are now in quarantine and being monitored, Tedros said.
